facts.fact_text: At the material time all the applicants were members of an opposition party called the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan (PFPA).
During the period from 2011 to 2013, all the applicants participated in a number of peaceful opposition demonstrations.
According to the applicants, they had intended to participate in upcoming protests planned by Milli Shura, including a protest scheduled for 9 March 2014, which was eventually cancelled.
The fourth applicant was an organiser of a protest scheduled for 23 February 2014.
According to the fourth applicant, he had created a Facebook group calling for the resignation of the Baku city mayor.
The Facebook group created by the fourth applicant had invited the public to participate in a demonstration against the Baku city mayor.
In the course of many of the peaceful opposition demonstrations, most of the applicants were arrested and subsequently convicted, as the assemblies had not been authorised.
All the applicants were arrested in either February or March 2014.
At the respective police stations or offices, administrative offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued against the applicants, setting out the charges against them.
All the applicants were charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The courts convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).

The European Parliament in its Resolution (2015/2840(RSP)) of 10 September 2015 emphasised that peaceful protesters have been effectively banned from demonstrating in central Baku since 2006.

The European Parliament in its Resolution (2015/2840(RSP)) of 10 September 2015 emphasised that new, harsh fines and longer periods of administrative detention for those who organise or participate in unauthorised public gatherings have recently been introduced in Azerbaijan.

Amnesty International in its Report of May 2014, titled 'Behind Bars: Silencing Dissent in Azerbaijan', referred to a decrease of public protests in Azerbaijan due to the harshening from 1 January 2013 of penalties for breach of rules on organisation and holding of peaceful assemblies.

Amnesty International in its Report of May 2014, titled 'Behind Bars: Silencing Dissent in Azerbaijan', emphasised that those who have called for public protest in Azerbaijan have been dealt with harshly, with criminal proceedings initiated against them under fabricated charges.
According to the applicants, they were never served with copies of the administrative offence reports or with other documents from their case files.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrest or while they were in police custody.
According to all the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing during the court proceedings before the first-instance courts.
The applicants complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that the hearings before the respective first-instance courts had not been fair.
